content:
We're happy to announce a public preview of the upcoming Lean language reference manual! After a lot of work on the technical foundations, we think that enough content is now present that it's more useful than the existing one, but I'd like to give you the chance to let me know if I've missed something important before the changeover.

You can see the preview release at https://lean-lang.org/doc/reference/latest/ (this will be the address of the final release as well).

The goal of the reference manual is to be a reference. This means that it's probably not a good place to learn Lean (unless you're already a skilled user of related technologies), but it should describe Lean comprehensively and accurately. If you already know Lean, but aren't sure about a detail, the reference is the place to go.

Barring any showstoppers, the plan is that the current language manual (that is, the content listed under "Language Manual" at https://lean-lang.org/lean4/doc/) will be replaced by the new one at the beginning of November. The setup guide, FAQ, and development guides will not be affected at this time.

This new reference has been rebuilt from the ground up in Verso. This means that all example code is type checked, the source code contains tests to ensure that it stays up-to-date with respect to changes in Lean, and we can add any features that we need to improve the documentation. Verso also makes it easy to integrate tightly with Lean, so we can show function docstrings directly, mechanically check descriptions of syntax against the actual parser, and insert cross-references automatically.

In the coming weeks, I'll be working on adding high-priority content, fixing issues that we identify, and improving the integration with Lean. Some of the very long documentation hovers will be getting shorter in an upcoming release as content is migrated to the text of the manual, with suitable links added to docstrings.

This reference manual is here to help you, the users of Lean. I'm very interested in hearing how it can better serve your needs. The best place to tell me about this is in the issue tracker at https://github.com/leanprover/reference-manual/issues, but if something doesn't seem to make sense as an issue, please feel free to ping me here. One of my goals with this text is that, when users ask technically interesting questions here on Zulip, dropping links to the language reference will be a suitable way to answer. 

The eventual goal is that datatype documentation resembles the chapter for strings, and that syntax/tactic documentation is like that for tactics. If there are ways to make these more useful for you, please don't hesitate to let me know - better to improve the template now than after I've written eight more chapters, after all! There's a few known caveats:

  • Rendered Markdown docstrings don't yet have Lean highlighting.

  • Docstrings are included as-is. Some are missing, and others are written inconsistently.

  • The CSS has not yet been optimized for mobile browsers.

No need to report these.

As usual for core Lean repositories, please discuss any large PRs before working on them. We're aiming for a consistent authorial voice, and not all conventions used in the text are explicitly documented yet. It may take more time to edit contributed text to match the rest of the document than it would take to write it from scratch, but it's no fun as a contributor to spend a lot of time on some text that ends up not being used. The most valuable contributions are high-quality illustrative examples, which can be posted in the reference manual's issue tracker. Your issue comments and upvotes will also be a very important input into the content planning and prioritization process. PRs that fix obvious typos are welcome without prior discussion or issues, but please don't submit too many in one PR, as that makes them much more time-consuming to review.

Thank you for your patience as I've been working on this!
Please direct your comments to the discussion thread so we don't clog everyone's notifications.

I've just posted what I believe will be the last preview prior to the new reference manual replacing the old one. Thank you all for your feedback on the navigation and layout - it's much better than it was in the first preview!

This time around, the display on mobile devices has been greatly improved. If you read documentation on your phone or tablet, please give it a spin and let me know on the issue tracker or the discussion thread if you encounter difficulties.

Significant new content:

  • Type classes
  • Notations and Macros

Just as with last time, please direct your comments to the discussion thread so we don't clog everyone's notifications.

We’re excited to announce that the new Lean reference manual is officially released, just in time for your holiday projects!

The reference manual will be a comprehensive, concise, and accurate description of Lean. Even though it’s not yet complete, it does contain descriptions of the tactic language, the most important parts of the term language, inductive datatypes and structures, and details about the elaboration process.

In the coming months, we'll be adding new content, prioritized according to my best understanding of Lean’s users’ needs. You can best influence that understanding by creating or upvoting issues in the repository. Issues for particular documentation topics are also a great place to describe what you presently need to know or are confused about so we can make sure the text answers your questions.

We’d like to thank you all for your feedback on the preview of the reference manual. As a result, it’s become much nicer to navigate. If you encounter difficulties with the organization or the UI, please open an issue or get in touch with me here.

There’s a few technical caveats with this first release:

  • The included API references are Lean docstrings. We will go through them to harmonize their language use and structure and better integrate them with the reference manual, but we have not yet done so.
  • Lean code in docstrings is not yet reliably syntax-highlighted or elaborated. This will improve.
  • The index is still at the early stages. Topic-specific indices will be implemented soon, and better search functionality is already under development.

In the near future, the contents of the reference manual will track Lean development. Once we believe that it’s comprehensive enough for this to make sense, we’ll begin making release-specific snapshots, but for now we think that resources are better spent on building out the content.

As with the public previews, please direct your comments to the discussion thread so we don't clog everyone's notifications.

In connection with the imminent Lean v4.17.0-rc1, the latest update to the reference manual has been released.

Since the prior release, the following has changed:

  • The new partial_fixpoint feature in v4.17.0-rc1 is documented
  • Well-founded recursion, Lake, and quotient types are now described in the reference manual, and the description of structural recursion has been greatly improved.
  • Descriptions and API references for all fixed-width integer types, Int, Fin, Empty, and Option were added.
  • Markdown in docstrings that contains code examples is now parsed and elaborated according to a variety of heuristics, resulting in clickable links and hovers in the rendered text.

Additionally, there's now a quick jump box to quickly navigate to a specific topic. Rather than being a full-text search, it takes advantage of Verso's database of documented topics to provide quick access to function documentation, tactics, syntax documentation, technical terminology, section headers, and other meaningful units. Please let me know how it works for you so it can get even better. Here's how it looks:

Screenshot of quick jump box

As usual, please direct your comments to the discussion thread so we don't clog everyone's notifications.

A new snapshot of the reference manual has been released!

This release features a visual overhaul that both improves the navigation features and makes the manual look much better. Each page now includes an overview in its table of contents that includes all of the documented syntax and names on the page.

There's also plenty of new content:

  • Interacting with Lean via commands such as #eval and #check
  • A description of the coercions mechanism
  • A description of the preprocessing mechanism for well-founded recursion that automatically introduces attach
  • The remaining basic types, including but not limited to Sum, Prod,Subtype, Sigma, List, Float, BitVec, and Thunk
  • Standard proposition and predicate formers, such as equality, conjunction, disjunction, implication, and quantifiers

As usual, please direct your comments to the discussion thread so we don't clog everyone's notifications.

Another snapshot of the reference manual is out! Once again, there are improvements to the look and feel of the generated HTML, especially on smaller screens and mobile devices.

In this snapshot, much of the included API reference documentation from Lean itself has been revised. It now includes more examples, and many missing docstrings have been added. The style of the docstrings has also been harmonized. The manual now includes the release notes for all versions of Lean 4.

These snapshots have been arriving rapidly as the manual converges towards its first proper release. And today is no different - a new snapshot is up!

Since the last preview, the following content has been added:

  • A chapter on Elan and its command line interface
  • A description of reference counting and memory management
  • Details about the specifics of unsafe and partial definitions
  • A detailed description of signatures and automatic implicit parameters
  • More details about reducibility
  • Nested inductive types
  • Axioms

The table of contents has also been reworked to better organize the information and make it easier to find.

In addition, more of the included docstrings have been edited upstream in Lean itself, and the manual is now generated with the latest nightly release of Lean.

As is usual, please direct discussions to the dedicated thread.

Thank you all for your helpful feedback!
